# Area claims

The register of who is working where, so no two sessions edit the same paths at
once. Established 2026-07-31 as step 2 of the parallel-development move
(`PARALLELISM.md`, "What to build first"). A text file and a rule; no tooling.

## The rules, in short

- **Claim your area before you edit its paths.** Append a `## CLAIM` block below.
  A claim keeps other sessions out of the paths it names; it is not a courtesy.
- **A session that needs work inside another area's claim DELEGATES.** Append a
  `## DELEGATION` block naming what you need and why, and continue with your own
  work. The owning area picks it up. Do not edit a claimed path quietly.
- **Release a claim explicitly**, by setting `released:` to the date. An
  unreleased claim older than its expected scope is stale, and `ARCH` may
  reassign it; silence does not hold ground forever.
- **Unclaimed paths are nobody's** — a collision risk, not a licence. Claim
  before editing even briefly.
- **Append only.** States are added, never edited in place, so the history of who
  held what is readable the same way the record's own history is. The one field
  that changes on an existing block is `released:`.

The format is the one `PARALLELISM.md` fixes:

```
## CLAIM <date> <AREA>
session: <name>
opened: <ISO8601>
paths: <comma-separated paths this claim reserves>
interfaces consumed: <ID(s), or none>
interfaces owned: <ID(s), or none>
expected: <the work this claim covers>
released: <date, or blank while live>
```

## DELEGATION 2026-07-31 UI → RECORD
from: ui-agent-7 (UI-7, the members & governance roster)
need: op=memberlist (or a sibling read) to carry each member's PROJECT OWNERSHIP — e.g. an `owns: [{ projectId, title }]` projection per member row. UI-7's roster must show "who owns which project" (core accountability: ownership is power, Section 7), but op=memberlist today returns only member_id/cover/handle/role/status/capabilities/invite_pending/expertise — no ownership. There is also no op that LISTS a member's projects. So the surface answers ownership by a BOUNDED FAN-OUT: it reads the record's project bundles (op=list) and calls op=projectparticipants for each, inverting owner→member on `handle`. That is an N+1 over projects and degrades honestly (a project it cannot read is skipped, never guessed; if projects cannot be listed at all the roster says ownership "not read" rather than implying nobody owns anything). A single `owns` projection on op=memberlist would remove the fan-out and make ownership a first-class roster fact rather than a join the UI reconstructs.
why: not blocking — UI-7 shipped the roster + ownership proven against the ops that exist (op=memberlist + op=projectparticipants over op=list), and the fan-out is bounded and honest. RECORD owns store.mjs and I3; whether to promote ownership onto the roster read (and the exact shape) is RECORD's call. Related: op=adminarith counts the founding administrator (the ADMIN_TOKEN holder), who has NO members row, so the roster and the governance denominator legitimately disagree on the administrator count; UI-7 reconciles this on-screen (founderReconcileHtml) rather than asking the plane to change — noted here only so RECORD knows the roster is deliberately not the whole administrator set.
status: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-04 by UI-16 — nothing consumes it any more, and RECORD should not build it. The fan-out this delegation existed to remove was DELETED with its surface: UI-16 took the roster's `Owns` column out and moved the question onto the project workspace, where `op=projectparticipants` answers it EXACTLY, in ONE call, for the one project the member is looking at. The `owns` projection would have made a cross-project participation view a first-class roster fact — which is the shape REC-25 had just made the plane's to gate — so removing the join is better than promoting it. If a future surface genuinely needs "which projects does this member own", it should be raised then, against that surface, and gated as a project read rather than as a member field.

## DELEGATION 2026-08-04 DIST → RECORD
from: dist1-agent / DIST-1 (the credential half of the REC-26 delegation)
need: a scoped `MONITOR_TOKEN` cannot be minted by the installer alone, and minting it alone would BREAK monitoring on every instance that received it. `bio-plane/src/store.mjs`'s `#monitorToken()` returns `env.MONITOR_TOKEN || env.ADMIN_TOKEN` — MONITOR_TOKEN FIRST — but `bio-plane/src/index.mjs`'s `classify()` recognises exactly three token values (`ADMIN_TOKEN`, `MEMBER_TOKEN`, `PROBE_TOKEN`) and returns `null` for anything else. So an instance carrying a `MONITOR_TOKEN` secret would select it for every monitor fire and be refused by its own control plane, while `#monitorConfigured()` stayed TRUE — the alarm arms, every tick fires, every fire 401s, and the instance looks configured. That is strictly worse than today and worse than no binding at all, so DIST-1 did NOT mint it. Making the scoped credential real needs, in RECORD's I3 ground and in ONE change with the installer's:
  1. `classify()` in bio-plane/src/index.mjs returns a `monitor` class for `env.MONITOR_TOKEN` (through `liveToken`, as the other three go);
  2. `OPS.monitor.classes` accepts it, and the archive arm of `op=acquire` (the `cls !== "admin" && cls !== "probe"` gate, whose comment already says "an operator or DAEMON credential") accepts it — and NOTHING else does, which is the whole point of the scoping;
  3. `scopeFor()` must NOT confine it to `scratch` (monitoring writes the live record, which is why PROBE_TOKEN is not the answer here);
  4. `op=selftest`'s binding report and `livefire.mjs`'s token-name list learn it, `tokens.mjs`'s `PUBLISHED_TOKEN_HASHES` covers any value that ever lands in the repo (the discipline is per-VALUE, not per-name, so no list edit is needed unless a MONITOR_TOKEN value is ever published);
  5. `CAPABILITIES.md` §4/§5: a fourth token CLASS is not a fifth capability token, but it is a doctrine-visible change and should be stated there rather than discovered.
When (1)-(4) land, DIST binds `{ type: "secret_text", name: "MONITOR_TOKEN", text: rand(32) }` in `uploadInstall` and mints-if-absent on `uploadUpdate` (the update path cannot read an existing secret back, so an update either always overwrites it or never sets it — that choice is DIST's and is a one-line change once the class exists).
why: least privilege. Today every monitor tick and every archive fallback on every installed instance runs under ADMIN_TOKEN — the root of trust for every membership rule (§4.6) — to do two narrow things: `op=monitor` on a bundle, and the archive arm of `op=acquire`. A leaked daemon credential is currently a total instance compromise; scoped, it is a monitoring nuisance. DEC-5's token-exposure surface is the standing context.

## DELEGATION 2026-08-04 RECORD → UI
from: rec18-agent / REC-18 (the earned basis grades)
need: two lines in `civicos-ui/app.html` — add `"capture"` to `GRADE_SOURCES` (~:1135), and give it a `GRADE_SOURCE_WORD`. `civicos-ui/check-semantics.mjs` currently FAILS against the worktree catalog with the exact message pair: `GRADE_SOURCES has drifted from the catalog` and `GRADE_SOURCE_WORD has no member-facing word for 'capture'`. It is a guard, not a break: it exists so a new grade source cannot reach a member surface as a blank sentence, and it named the whole migration for you.
why: REC-18 makes the CAPTURE axis earned from the capture record rather than authored, and before this there was no source name meaning that — all four existing sources were sources for a CONNECTION grade, so a capture-axis leg had to borrow a connection word and nothing checked its value against the record. The measured consequence was that a member could type capture grade A beside a document, against the landed doctrine that grade A needs a chain-of-custody archive this plane cannot produce and does not claim (CAPTURE-FIDELITY.md, RECONCILED R2-e/R2-g).
wording, as a suggestion and not a ruling (the member-facing word is UI's): something that says what the grade IS — a fact about how the bytes reached us, held by the record — e.g. "from the capture record". It must NOT read as a member's assertion, or it collapses into `testimony`'s meaning. And `capture` and `resolution` must NOT be rendered as one "earned" badge: they are earned from two different things over two different populations, and DEC-21 is that the axes are never composed.
also available, and UI-20/UI-21 will want it: `op=earnedbasis&id=<inquiry>[&targets=a,b,c]` answers what each candidate leg earns BEFORE it is written — `{subject_entity, subject_label, earned: {connection: {<target>: {grade, mode: 'value', why}}, capture: {<target>: {grade, mode: 'ceiling', why, ceiling}}}}`. It answers from the SAME store function op=promote enforces with, so what it reports is what the write will accept. A cite flow should FILL the leg from it rather than offering a grade control the member can type into.
filed as: IC-11 in `INTERFACE-CHANGES.md` (PROPOSED — UI is a LIVE consumer here, so silence is not consent).

from: ui22-agent / UI-22 (the five pre-DEC-8 refusal residues)
need: publish the CAPTURE-DIRECTED acts the way `op=affordances` publishes object-directed ones — at minimum `attest`, with its `label`, its `needs` and its `rung`. It does not have to join `ACTS` and probably should not: a shape beside `catalog` in the no-target answer (a `capture_acts` block, or `non_acts` decorated with what `decorateAct` already computes) is enough, because what a surface needs is the producer's own NAME for the act and the capability it takes, not a per-object derivation.
why: UI-22 rewired the document page's three act sections off their surface-side rules and onto the publication. TWO of them landed clean — `release` and `dispose` are published acts, so their sections now exist exactly where the record publishes them, under the record's own labels, and the two sentences that used to explain their absence are deleted. THE THIRD COULD NOT, and the reason is the plane's doctrine rather than a shortcut: `attest` is a NON_ACT in `affordances.mjs` ("capture-directed: co-attestation of a capture's existence in time"), so the answer carries no entry, no label, no `needs` and no `rung` for it on any target. So `Co-attest this capture…` is still a name this surface invented for an act the record owns, and `canAttest()` is still a surface-side copy of `op=attest`'s NEEDS (`contribute`, read out of index.mjs). Both are the last of the class UI-12 opened, and neither can be closed from this side.

The same is true of `ratify`. So the rung half is a publication change and not a new determination; only the LABEL is new wording, and it is the record's to choose because it is the record's act.
do NOT: fold `attest` into `ACTS`. The NON_ACTS entry states a real distinction — an act whose subject is a capture sha is not an act on a bundle — and collapsing it would make `op=affordances?target=<bundle>` publish an act that is not about that bundle, which is the pre-flight-disagreeing-with-the-refusal failure DEC-8 exists to forbid.

## DELEGATION 2026-08-05 UI → RECORD

raised by: ui39-agent (worktree agent-ac6c0018a3d94d2c5), UI-39
what UI needs: **two read ops publish a bound they do not name, so a surface has to assert its own.** `op=search` gets this right — it answers `total`, `limit` and `offset` beside the page, which is exactly what let UI-39 fix `heldMatch` by walking the plane's own count. Two of its siblings do not:
  1. **`op=readingname` (`documentsNamingEntity`, store.mjs ~7583)** caps at `Math.min(Number(limit) || 100, 500)` and returns `count` — *the length of what it sent*, which is indistinguishable from the length of what exists. It publishes NO `limit` and NO truncation flag. So `loadResolveCandidates` cannot read the bound off the answer, and UI-39 shipped the honest half available to a surface: it SETS `limit` and states the number it ASKED FOR. That sentence is true whatever the plane clamps to (a clamp can only make the list shorter than the claim, UI-26's conservative direction) but it is a bound the surface authored, not one the record published. **Asked for: `limit` (the cap actually applied) and `truncated` on the answer.** Then the sentence states the record's own figure and the surface stops asserting one.
  2. **`op=tasks` (`taskList`, store.mjs ~15194)** caps at 200 and publishes a `counts` block whose figures count the whole visible set — but no truncation flag, where its sibling `op=queue` publishes `truncated` explicitly. UI-39 therefore INFERS the resolutions bound from the arithmetic (`counts.resolved` against the rows delivered) and words it as the inference it is, kept deliberately distinct from the queue's line, which quotes the record's own flag. **Asked for: `truncated` on `op=tasks`, matching `op=queue`.**
why it is not fixed here: `bio-plane/**` is RECORD's ground and this session opened none of it — the zero-byte battery delta is the evidence.
severity: neither is a correctness defect today. Both are the same shape as the class UI-39 exists to close, one layer down: **a producer that caps without publishing the cap forces every consumer to guess or to assert.** Two surfaces have now had to.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-07 UI -> RECORD (the investigative-session area): NO OP LISTS RUNS BY CONTEXT

**What is needed:** an op that answers *which runs are attached to this inquiry or project* — `op=airuns&contextType=<inquiry|project>&contextId=<id>`, gated on `context_id` through the same `#bundleGate` `aiRunRead` already uses, publishing the same `session` shape per row, and **bounded with its bound PUBLISHED** (`limit`/`truncated`, REC-59/REC-60's pair) because a context may accumulate runs without limit.

**Why it is not optional.** `INVESTIGATIVE-SESSION.md` §14a promises that *any window focused on an inquiry or a project* shows the indicator, and names the price explicitly: *"a teammate watching the running-session indicator can see that work is happening and cannot read the reasoning."* **A teammate is the case this op is for.** Today `op=airun` and `op=airunlog` are both keyed by run id, so a window can only ask about a run whose address it already holds — and the member who already holds the address is precisely the member who did not need telling. UI-49 built the call site and every value on it comes from the record; what it cannot build is the question.

**What UI-49 shipped in the meantime, and why it is honest rather than a stand-in:** the window resolves the addresses THIS DEVICE has already opened, and asks the record about each one. The device supplies an ADDRESS and nothing else; the label, the status and **whether the run belongs to this window at all** are the record's answers. When the op lands, `aiSessionContextHtml` is the one function that changes — the call sites, the renderers and every pin over them stay.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-07 UI -> RECORD: `op=airunlog` PUBLISHES AN UNBOUNDED COLLECTION

`store.mjs` `aiRunLog` runs `SELECT ... FROM ai_run_log WHERE run = ? ORDER BY seq` with **no LIMIT, no `limit` and no `truncated`** — an append-only log read whole. That is REC-57/REC-59's boundedness class, and it is the reason UI-49 DECIDED the observation log is a SEPARATE surface rather than the indicator's click-through (the reasoning is at the site, in `app.html`'s `__AI_SESSION__` block). A UI built against it today would be a surface with a bound it cannot state, which is exactly what UI-46 spent an item removing.

**What this costs UI, named precisely rather than left to be discovered.** `civicos-ui/check-semantics.mjs` computes `CANONICAL = [...new Set(Object.values(OBJECT_TYPES))]` and requires an entry for every canonical type in **SEVEN** tables inside `app.html`: `PREFIX`, `FIRST_STATE`, `HEADINGS`, `SCHEMA_OF`, `STATE_EDGES`, `TYPE_LABEL` and `SEMANTICS.types`. **`node civicos-ui/test/run.mjs` will fail with seven `has no entry for the catalog type 'bias'` lines until those are added.** The bio-plane battery is unaffected and is green at 111/111 — `check-semantics.mjs` is run only from `civicos-ui/test/run.mjs`.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 VERIFY -> REC-64 / whoever allocates the next DEC-49 ROW: WHAT A `where` NOW MEANS

**A `where` names the SMALLEST SPAN in which the row's refusal is enforced, and the guard judges exactly that span and nothing else.** Two spellings, and the second is new:

- `<file> <fn>` — the whole function body is the governed site. **Correct ONLY when every refusal that function makes is your family's business.**
- `<file> <fn> > <region>` — a NAMED REGION inside it, delimited in the source by `DEC-49 REGION <name>` / `END DEC-49 REGION <name>` block comments.

**It is stated in three places, all of which a next allocator will meet:** a "WHAT A `where` MEANS" block at the head of the DEC-49 families in `bio-plane/checks/bio-checks.mjs`; the two rows' own comments (`BASIS_VERSION_CHECKS.VERSION_FROZEN`, `.VERSION_LEG_UNRESOLVED`); and `parseWhere`'s header in `civicos-ui/check-refusal-codes.mjs`. **The guard also says it in the failure itself** — a not-a-row failure at a whole-function `where` now adds *"if the row governs only an arm of it, the fix is a REGION `where` and not a translation for this code"*, because that is the wrong turn REC-71 exists to prevent and the failure message is where it will actually be read.

**WIDENING A `where` WIDENS WHAT MUST BE TRANSLATED TODAY.** If you find yourself widening one to cover a refusal, you are doing REC-64's sweep in the worst possible place. Add the row, or narrow the `where`.

**Every way a region can be wrong FAILS** — missing, unclosed, duplicated, inside out, outside the function it names, trivially short, judging no refusal at all, or declared in the source with no `where` claiming it. ### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 FLEET -> whoever builds FL-3: THE SEGMENT IS SIZED, AND CPU IS NOT WHAT SIZES IT

**FL-3 should be shaped against MEMORY, not against the CPU ceiling.** Measured 2026-08-08 on a deployed probe, platform-observed (`MEASUREMENTS.md`, the FL-1 entry):

- **Waiting is effectively free.** 25 subrequests each held open 2 s — 50.0 s of wall time — cost **4.29 ms** of billed CPU, about **0.16 ms per awaited subrequest regardless of how long the wait lasts**. So a segment that suspends on the daemon costs nothing to be suspended, and §14a's resumable shape carries no CPU penalty at all.
- **CPU per turn grows as ~n^1.9** — 24.29 ms at 25 turns, 189.28 ms at 100, 4,488.9 ms at 400 — because the whole transcript is re-serialised every turn. Extrapolated on the measured exponent, ~1,100 turns fit the 30 s default and ~3,700 the 5-minute maximum.
- **BUT MEMORY REACHES 120.4 MB OF THE 128 MB ISOLATE AT 200 TURNS**, while CPU is still 2.5% of the ceiling. **That is the wall, and it arrives roughly ten times sooner than the CPU wall.** 400-turn invocations still completed, so it is pressure rather than a kill — but a segment sized on CPU headroom would be sized about an order of magnitude too long.
- **A segment of 100–150 model turns sits comfortably inside both**, on this corpus — and the corpus is a FLOOR: one development instance's real op bodies, where a loaded instance's `projection` and `search` are larger.
- **The cheapest single change if a longer segment is ever wanted: stop re-serialising the whole transcript every turn.** Both the CPU exponent and the memory curve come from that one behaviour — not from the waiting, and not from the payload sizes.

**And one hard constraint FL-2/FL-3 must not rediscover:** a Worker CANNOT reach another Worker on this account's own `*.workers.dev` name — **404, body `error code: 1042`, in 7 ms, every time**. The **service binding** to the same script answered 200 and honoured a 1,500 ms delay. That is I6's pattern already, so nothing about the design changes — but a fleet member built to call the plane by URL fails in a way that looks like anything except routing. It cost this session two probe passes.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 FLEET -> whoever runs D-224: YOUR MEASUREMENT IS NOW THE ONE THAT MOVES D-190

`op=affordances` now publishes six object-directed acts on an inquiry — `versionaccept`, `versionreject`, `versionconsider`, `versionrevert`, `versioncurrent`, `versionhide`. **`civicos-ui/test/surface-registry.test.mjs` ARM A4 fails naming all six**, because its rule is that every act the plane publishes is hosted by a described surface and none of them is yet.

**That arm is RIGHT and PL-2 deliberately did not silence it.** Describing a surface that does not exist would be the registry lying about what a member can reach, which is the one thing the registry is for. The three items that build the surfaces — **UI-42** (version review: rotation and diff, the prune offer's wording), **UI-43** (the accept ceremony, the four beats, the per-branch affirmation) and **UI-45** (the aged/aggregated suggestion feed) — all list PL-2 as a dependency, and PL-2 is now landed, so all three are unblocked.

**What UI needs from the plane and already has, so nothing is owed back:**

- **The machine is PUBLISHED, not copied.** `op=affordances` answers `vocabularies.version_states`, `vocabularies.version_edges` and `vocabularies.version_reason_required`. **Read them; do not restate them.** The edge table is what says whether "put this back" is offerable at all, and `version_reason_required` is what says WHEN a surface must collect a reason BEFORE it sends the act — without it a member types a reason into a form that discards it, or worse, is refused after the fact.
- **BEAT 2 of the four beats is a real op parameter.** Every one of the six accepts `preview=1` (and `preview=true`), runs **every** guard, writes nothing, and returns either the refusal the act would return or `{ ok:true, preview:true, wrote:false, from, to }`. It is the same code path up to the write, so the pre-flight cannot disagree with the act. **Use it for the ceremony's "here is what will happen" step rather than composing a prediction.**
- **Every refusal carries a C-number, a DEC-49 wire code and a canned translation.** Render the translation; never compose one.
- **Hidden and settled readings are RETURNED AND FLAGGED, never filtered** (D-214, DEC-29(b)). The display shrinks; the query still answers. `op=basisversions` also carries `moved: { by, at, reason }` per version, which is the rejection record UI-45's feed and UI-42's history both want.
- **`op=versioncurrent` requires `project=` and there is no default.** A surface must name which project is moving its stance, and the plane refuses `VERSION_CURRENT_NO_PROJECT` otherwise — §7, so one team's decision never quietly moves another's. `op=basisversions&project=<PROJ>` answers what THAT project stands on.

**One wording bound worth carrying into the surfaces:** no member-facing string in this item says "ground", "partition", "AND" or "OR" as a member-facing word (DEC-32's elicitation clause 1, D-226), and the suite asserts it of every translation. The published act LABELS follow the same bound and are the plane's own words — render them.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> BOB, via CONDUCT: **A BACKGROUND RUN CANNOT PROPOSE A READING THAT RESTS ON DOCUMENTS, AND THAT IS A PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN A BUG**

**MEASURED, not inferred, and found by driving the endpoint rather than by reading the design.** PL-1's `C-25.5` makes a version's structure TOTAL — *"a version does not get the not-at-all arm, because §3 requires it to CARRY the partition"* — so **every** version carrying legs declares at least one part. PL-1's `C-25.15` then requires every declared part to be asserted by a **named member**, because *"these legs are enough on their own" is an authored judgment that makes the finding STRONGER*. Both rules are right and both are landed.

**Together they mean a machine credential can write §9's `level-empty` kind and cannot write a reading that rests on a single document.** PL-3 refuses that BY NAME (`C-27.13`) so the caller is told which act it is short of, rather than composing a document and meeting `C-25.15` at the write in another family's words. The **interactive mode (§10) runs under a named member and can propose all five kinds**, which is why the item's acceptance is met; the **background job (§10's first mode) is narrower than the design reads**.

- **Provisional:** refuse the machine by name at the endpoint; the background job proposes empty-level findings and the interactive session proposes everything.
- **Why it was ambiguous:** §5 says the session *composes* legs and §14b.5 lists checks that presuppose legged machine-composed versions; PL-1's own `C-25.15` message says *"a machine-composed version PROPOSES the structure rather than asserting it"* — anticipating exactly this and leaving no shape in which it can.
- **Alternative:** a version with EXACTLY ONE part asserts nothing beyond what its legs already say — the OR-maximum is what makes a part-assertion load-bearing, and with one part there is no maximum to take. Exempting the single-part case from `C-25.15` would let a background run propose an unstructured (implicit-AND, weakest-leg) reading, which is DEC-32's conservative default and cannot overstate anything.
- **Recommendation: TAKE THE ALTERNATIVE, but not in this item.** It edits a landed check of PL-1's on which PL-2 and PL-14 both build, and widening PL-3 to reach a neighbouring rule is the mistake REC-71 exists to correct. It belongs in the item that schedules the background mode — **FL-3**, which is the first thing that will actually run unattended.
- **Reversal cost:** low today and rising. Nothing has been written under the current rule, so relaxing it later costs one check arm and one suite arm. Once a corpus carries machine-proposed readings the relaxation is still safe (it only ever admits more), but the reverse — tightening it — would strand them.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> FL-3 (the run harness): **WHAT THE HARNESS INHERITS, AND THE ONE THING IT MUST NOT REBUILD**

- **`op=suggest` is the ONE write.** One endpoint for both modes; the composition goes in the POST body; `author` and `viewer` are server-stamped and a caller-supplied value is deleted at the control plane.
- **F10's `denied-means-adjust` has a plane-side half already built, and the harness owns the other half.** A verbatim resubmit is a STRUCTURAL NO-OP — the stored refusal comes back with `evaluated: false`, `repeated: true`, `wrote: false` and a `repeats` count, no second evaluation, no document touched. **So the harness's table row is about ADJUSTING, not about avoiding churn: the churn is already gone.** `repeats` climbing is the signal that a run is looping without adjusting, and it is visible to something other than the budget.
- **Every refusal carries a C-number, a DEC-49 wire code and a canned translation. RENDER the translation; never compose one.**
- **The kind `level-empty` is what an empty run emits**, and FL-3's owed control 7 (an inquiry the evidence does not support proposes NOTHING and emits §9's empty-level kind) has its object to count: the kind is a column on `inquiry_basis_versions`, readable through `op=basisversions`.
- **Do NOT rebuild the pre-write checks fleet-side.** SWEEP C11 and §14b.5 are explicit that they are the PLANE'S; a fleet-side copy is the drift class DEC-8 closed. The fleet member receives verdicts.
- **The bound REFUSES rather than truncates.** `SUGGEST_LEGS_MAX` is 120 and a submission over it is turned away naming the bound, so a harness splits a reading rather than discovering a silent cut.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> PL-4 and PL-11: **WHAT EACH INHERITS, AND WHAT THIS ITEM DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD**

- **PL-4 (`capture_requests`).** This item writes **no capture request and no capture**. §4 group 1 is untouched. `suggest_refusals` is the shape PL-4's table should copy — scratch-class, in `capture_sessions`' family, before the `host_governor` block, in `purge` in BOTH arms and counted by `op=stats` — and the trap to copy with it is that **a table keyed on something other than `bundle_id` cannot ride purge's `TABLES` list and needs its own DELETE in each arm** (D-113 arriving through a column name).
- **PL-11 (the `ai` credential class).** `op=suggest` rides `["admin", "member", "probe"]` today and PL-11 **narrows** it — the direction IS-6 recorded as the safe one. Note what the fence here does NOT depend on: the class list is not what stops a machine settling a reading. `MACHINE_CANNOT_MOVE_VERSION` (PL-2) and `SUGGEST_UNWRITABLE_STATE` (this item) both refuse **by shape** through REC-46's one predicate, so `token:ai` is caught the day it exists without either of them being edited. PL-11's `MACHINE_CANNOT_*` sweep should include **`SUGGEST_UNWRITABLE_STATE`**, which is a `MACHINE_CANNOT_` rule wearing a different name because it refuses a *structural assertion* rather than a *transition*.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> REC-64 / whoever next narrows a `where`: **THE UNFALSIFIABLE-GOVERNED-SITE TREND HAS A CHEAP, GENERAL FIX, AND IT IS MEASURED**

REC-71 measured that **7 of 13 governed sites read 776 lines and compared ZERO codes**, and that *"every family since VF-2 has added them and the ratio is getting worse."* The cause is mechanical: arm C compares a code against its family only when it can SEE the code, and a local `refuse(key, …)` helper passes the code as a **variable**.

**The fix is to name the local helper `refusal` and pass the code as a STRING LITERAL at every site.** Arm C already matches `refusal("CODE"` by name. PL-3 did this deliberately and the figure moved from **11 to 30 codes compared** across the whole plane — 19 of the 30 are PL-3's, and every one of its refusals is now falsifiable rather than merely read. The change is local to the site, costs nothing, and needs no guard edit.

**Two things the guard is still blind to and PL-3 could not fix from here:** `basisVersionFindings` (244 lines, 0 judged) and `checkBiasExtension` (158 lines, 0 judged) refuse by PUSHING findings rather than by returning `ok:false`, so no matcher sees them at all. That is a matcher gap rather than a naming one and belongs to whoever owns arm C.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> SK-3 (the PRACTICE-SURVEY prohibition set): **THE CODE HALF OF THE FIFTH PROHIBITION IS BUILT AND IT IS A BOUNDARY, NOT A PROSE JUDGE**

`isBoilerplate` and `BOILERPLATE_FORMS` are exported from `checks/bio-checks.mjs` — ONE predicate, one roster, no second membership test. `C-27.12` refuses a version whose description, claim, part-statement or leg note is filler, and the plan's own control for SK-3 ("submit a version whose description is placeholder text through PL-3 -> refused by C-number while the skill-only path would have passed it") is **RUN and green** in `test/suggest.test.mjs`.

**What it CANNOT do is stated at the predicate rather than implied**, on D-130's precedent: a machine that writes "the relevant department" gets past every rule in it. It matches the WHOLE field, case-folded and trimmed, **never as a substring** — a real finding that QUOTES a placeholder must land, and that over-strictness arm is driven. **The skill still owns the part the code cannot reach**, which is what SK-3's prohibition set is for.

### DELEGATION 2026-08-08 RECORD (PL-3) -> VF-1: **OWED CONTROL 6 IS RUN, RECORDED AND RE-RUNNABLE IN ONE STEP**

`node bio-plane/test/suggest.control.mjs` — TEN arms, all restored, every file verified by sha256 **and by content**. Six of them are VF-1's control 6 proper: **each of the six pre-write refusals neutered ALONE with the other five HELD OPEN**, each naming its own C-number, and each declaring what must **not** fail so a suite that failed "somewhere" could not pass for a suite that failed at the right place.

**Two arms did not behave as first declared, and both are findings rather than repairs:**

1. **Arm (6) predicted the DEC-49 floor would fail and it did not.** The floor measures a CODE's reachability, not a BRANCH's, and `C-27.13` has two producers — the arm neuters one and deliberately leaves the other live. The declaration was corrected; the control was right.
2. **Arm (8) left the suite GREEN at 59/59** — *a control that passes while asserting nothing*, in this item's own suite. The arm asserted that a registry ROW existed (its C-number and its `where`), which is true whether or not anything enforces it. **Corrected to DRIVE the refusal through `op=promote`**, and driving it immediately exposed a real defect: `promote`'s `BASIS_VERSION_REFUSED` looked its translation up in ONE registry, so the new document-gate code went out with `translation: undefined` — **an untranslated code reaching a member, which is exactly what DEC-49 ended, and the DEC-49 guard could not see it because the code is a variable at that site.**
